name: Acoustic Guitar
description: A steel-string, nylon-string or twelve-string acoustic guitar: plucked strings heard through a wooden body, played with a fingertip, a nail or a pick.

params.name: Type
params.description: Which guitar is played: bright steel strings, round nylon strings, or twelve strings in octave and unison pairs. It changes from the next note.

params.name: Body
params.description: How much of the wooden box is heard, from the bare string to the full body with its low thump at every pluck.

params.name: Position
params.description: Where the string is plucked, from close to the bridge, thin and nasal, to over the soundhole, round and hollow. It changes from the next note.

params.name: Nail
params.description: What plucks the string, from the soft pad of a finger to a nail to a hard pick. Higher is brighter, with a click at the start of each note.

params.name: Sustain
params.description: How long a held note rings. Low notes ring longer than high ones, and nylon dies away sooner than steel. It changes from the next note.

params.name: Release
params.description: How a note ends when the key is let go. Short is a finger stopping the string; long lets it ring on until it dies by itself.

params.name: Tone
params.description: The brightness of the whole instrument, from dark and woody to bright and glassy.

params.name: Shimmer
params.description: How fast each note slowly beats against itself, as a real string does. On twelve strings it is how far the paired strings are out of tune.

params.name: Strum
params.description: How far the notes of a chord are spread in time, low string first, like a hand moving across the strings. Single notes are never delayed.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Output level of the instrument. A soft clip after it rounds off the peaks when many notes stack up.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. A signal model of a flat-top acoustic guitar; it uses no samples and is not a model of any one instrument. Modelled: each note is two of the kit's plucked-string loops (extended Karplus-Strong, Jaffe-Smith lineage) for the string's two polarisations, one louder and shorter lived, one quieter and longer lived, which gives the two-stage decay and the slow beat of a real note; stiff steel against nylon that loses its highs sooner; the pluck point; a body of fixed resonances with the air mode near 100 Hz and the main top mode near 200 Hz; a knock into the body at every pluck. Simplified: one body for all three types, eight parallel resonances beside the direct string; the kit's one-pole string loss; polarisations that do not exchange energy; no string or fret assignment, no sympathetic strings; release is a fade behind a closing low-pass; a twelve-string course is one extra loop, an octave up below B3 and a unison above. Choices, not measurements: the six upper body modes, every Q and gain, the sustain law, the shares of the two polarisations, the inharmonicity, the damping exponents, the knock level, the strum step and the pluck-to-pluck variation.
